Fresh floods and landslides set off by heavy rain and storms have killed at least 14 people in Nepal and left another 11 missing, with authorities warning on Sunday that more flash floods were possible. The warnings covered 49 of Nepal's 77 districts, more than half of which faced a high risk of flooding, as water levels in major rivers kept rising. The video filmed at 5:30pm, local time, on Sunday, September 27 shows the latest destruction. Fortunately, no injuries were reported. However, it remains unclear whether the tourist will face legal action or be required to pay compensation. This isn't a scene from a film. This is a heartbreaking reality that still exists in parts of Nepal. For some women and girls, getting their period means being sent away from their own home to spend the night in a small shed, away from their families. They are left to face cold nights, fear, loneliness, and the danger of snakes, insects, and wild animals—all because of a natural biological process. Menstruation should never be a reason for exclusion or shame. Take a moment and ask yourself: If it were someone you love—your daughter, your sister, your wife, or your mother—would you accept this as "tradition"? Some customs deserve to be questioned, especially when they put lives and dignity at risk. Every woman deserves to feel safe, respected, and valued, no matter what day of the month it is. Let's raise awareness, start conversations, and stand together to end harmful practices like this. Nepal’s Finance Minister Dr. Swarnim Wagle held a direct discussion with Indian External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar at the NDTV World Summit 2026 in New Delhi, focusing on Nepal-India relations and regional cooperation. During the discussion, Wagle expressed Nepal’s gratitude for India’s swift assistance during recent disasters in Rasuwa and Bhotekoshi, as well as its support following Nepal’s devastating 2015 earthquake. Wagle also raised the possibility of strengthening cooperation between the two countries in disaster response, nutrition and clean energy. Responding to the discussion, Jaishankar emphasized the importance of formal partnerships and practical, results-oriented cooperation.  He cited the International Solar Alliance as an example of a framework that can support collaboration on shared priorities. The exchange highlighted opportunities for Nepal and India to deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in disaster preparedness, sustainable development and regional energy initiatives. 🇳🇵 WELCOME TO DASHAIN! Nepal’s biggest and most important Hindu festival, celebrated over 15 days! And ICONICALLY, it celebrates the victory of a powerful goddess over evil. 💅 According to Hindu mythology, Durga, the goddess of strength, courage and protection, battled the evil buffalo demon Mahishasura for nine days before defeating him on the tenth. A whole festival celebrating female power? I’M OBSESSED. 📍 Kathmandu Durbar Square — the historic heart of Kathmandu, home to centuries-old temples and palaces, many of which were badly damaged in the devastating 2015 earthquake and have since been restored. 👑 The Living Goddess (Kumari): Nepal has a tradition of worshipping a real-life young girl as the living embodiment of the goddess Taleju. The current Royal Kumari is just THREE YEARS OLD! She’s selected from a Buddhist family and revered by both Hindus and Buddhists. ❤️ Tika: During Dashain, families come together as elders place a red mixture of rice, yoghurt and vermilion on their loved ones’ foreheads, offering blessings for health, happiness and prosperity. And this is only the beginning of my Nepal adventure… In just a few days, this 34-year-old hag will be attempting to summit Mera Peak at 6,476 metres (21,247 ft) in the Himalayas! 🏔️ No gear, no idea, but plenty of ambition.
